note: Becomes *j'* before a vowel or a silent *h*: *j'ai, j'habite*.
For family, friends and children. Polite: *vous*.
Also *it* for masculine nouns: *le livre → il*.
Also *it* for feminine nouns: *la table → elle*. The same word means *her* after a preposition: *avec elle*.
In speech *on* usually means *we*: *On y va ?* = Shall we go? It takes the *il* form.
The same word is also *us*: *avec nous*.
Both *you all* and the polite *you*: *Vous êtes prêt ?*
For men, or a mixed group.
Only for women, or feminine nouns.
*moi, toi, lui, elle, nous, vous, eux, elles*: after prepositions and on their own: *Moi ?*
*à moi, à toi, à lui…* = mine, yours, his…
*te* = you (informal); the object pronoun goes before the verb.
*me* = me; *m'* before a vowel: *Il m'aime.*
*le* = him, or *it* for a masculine noun.
*la* = her, or *it* for a feminine noun.
*le* and *la* become *l'* before a vowel.
*les* = them.
*nous* = us.
*vous* = you.
*lui* = to him and to her.
*me* = (to) me.
*te* = (to) you (informal).
*leur* = to them.
Literally *does it please you*.

french: Il nous a dit la vérité.
note: *nous* = (to) us.
*y* = there, or *to it*: *J'y pense.* = I'm thinking about it.
*il y a* = there is, there are. With a time it means *ago*: *il y a deux jours*.
*en* = some, of it, of them.
*me, te, se, nous, vous, se*: *se lever* = to get up.
*se souvenir* = to remember.
Literally *we see each other tomorrow*.
*s'inquiéter* = to worry; *se* becomes *s'* before a vowel.
Agrees with the thing owned: *mon père, ma mère, mes parents*. *mon* also before a feminine word with a vowel: *mon amie*.
His or her, depending on the thing owned: *son père* = his father or her father.
The same word is also the pronoun *to them*: *Je leur écris.*
The everyday greeting until the evening; always say it when you enter a shop.
Informal, for hello and goodbye.
Informal: *s'il te plaît*.
Informal: *Excuse-moi*.
*Je suis désolé* (*désolée* for a woman) = I'm sorry.
Answer: *Ça va (bien).* Longer: *Comment ça va ?*
Polite: *Et vous ?*
Literally *I call myself*.
Polite: *Comment vous appelez-vous ?*
A woman writes *enchantée*; it sounds the same.
Informal: *À plus !*, written *A+*.
Also *À la vôtre !* / *À la tienne !*
Contradicts a *no*: *Tu ne viens pas ? – Si !* = Aren't you coming? – Yes, I am! The same word is also *if*.
Around the verb: *Je ne sais pas.* In speech the *ne* is often dropped: *Je sais pas.*
*Je ne fume jamais.*
*Je ne vois rien.* Alone: *Rien.*
*Je ne connais personne.*
A woman says *fatiguée*: adjectives agree with the speaker.
Literally *is it true?*
Literally *I have hunger*.
*J'ai besoin d'aide.* = I need help.
Age with *avoir*: *Tu as quel âge ?*
*J'ai envie d'une glace.* = I feel like an ice cream.
*avoir mal à* = to hurt: *J'ai mal au dos.*
*le*: masculine.
*la*: feminine.
*l'* before a vowel or a silent *h*, masculine and feminine: *l'ami, l'amie, l'hôtel*.
*les*: every plural. Before a vowel its *s* is pronounced: *les amis* [lez-ami].
*un*: masculine.
*une*: feminine.
*des*: the plural of *un* and *une*; English often has no word for it.
*du* = *de* + *le*: for amounts of something you don't count.
After a negative *du, de la, des* become *de*: *Je n'ai pas de pain.*

english: à + le = to the, at the
note: *au cinéma*, *au restaurant*. *à la* and *à l'* don't merge.
*aux États-Unis*.

english: de + le = of the, from the
note: *le livre du professeur* = the teacher's book.
*à Paris*, *à la gare*, *à huit heures*.
*de Paris*; *un verre de vin* = a glass of wine. *d'* before a vowel.
*en France*, *en juin*, *en train*.
*dans la boîte*; *dans deux jours* = in two days.
*chez moi* = at my place; *chez le médecin* = at the doctor's.
*par la fenêtre*; *deux fois par jour* = twice a day.
*vers huit heures* = around eight.
*depuis deux ans* = for two years (and still going).
*pendant deux heures* = for two hours.
In speech often *here*: *Je suis là.* = I'm here.
The everyday *what* at the start: *Qu'est-ce que tu fais ?* After a verb or a preposition: *quoi* (*C'est quoi ?*).
With an accent; *ou* without one is *or*.
The same word is also *when* (connecting): *Quand il pleut, je reste à la maison.*
Answer: *parce que* = because.
*C'est combien ?* = How much is it?
Agrees: *quel, quelle, quels, quelles*: *Quelle heure est-il ?*
Turns a sentence into a question: *Est-ce que tu viens ?* In speech a rising voice is enough: *Tu viens ?*
*Tu viens d'où ?* = Where are you from?
*lequel, laquelle, lesquels, lesquelles*.
The everyday *that*: *Ça va ?*, *J'aime ça.*
*C'est bon.* Plural: *ce sont*.
*cet* before a vowel: *cet homme*. *-ci* and *-là* make it *this* or *that*: *ce livre-ci*.
Also *that's it*: *Voilà !*
*celui-ci, celle-ci, ceux-ci, celles-ci*; with *-là*: that one.
*tous les jours* = every day.
*beaucoup de monde* = a lot of people.
*un autre café* = another coffee; *l'autre jour* = the other day.
*la même chose* = the same thing; *même moi* = even me.
Without an accent; *où* is *where*.
*parce qu'* before a vowel.
*Alors, on y va ?* = So, shall we go?
*s'il* before *il/ils*: *s'il pleut* = if it rains. The same word is also *yes* to a negative question.
*comme toi* = like you; *Comme il pleut, …* = As it's raining, …
*encore une fois* = once more; *pas encore* = not yet.
*Il est toujours là.* = He's still here.

english: in a moment; a moment ago
note: *À tout à l'heure !* = See you soon!
Also *o'clock*: *Il est trois heures.*
*Bonne journée !* = Have a nice day!
With numbers: *trois ans*; *l'année* for a whole year or with an adjective: *toute l'année*.
In speech also *Il est quelle heure ?*
The 24-hour clock is common: *le train de quinze heures*.
*une* before a feminine noun: *une heure*.
*et* only with *un*: *vingt et un, trente et un*; otherwise a hyphen: *vingt-deux*.
Sixty-ten. In Belgium and Switzerland: *septante*.
Four twenties. The *s* goes when another number follows: *quatre-vingt-un*. In Switzerland also *huitante*.
Four twenties and ten. In Belgium and Switzerland: *nonante*.
Never takes an *s*: *deux mille*.
Followed by *de*: *un million d'euros*.
Feminine *première*; written *1er*, *1re*. Dates use plain numbers except the first: *le premier mai*, *le deux mai*.
The number + *-ième*, without its final *e*: *quatre → quatrième*.
*cinq* adds a *u*: *cinquième*.
*neuf* → *neuvième*: the *f* becomes *v*.
Days are masculine and written in lower case: *lundi* = on Monday; *le lundi* = on Mondays.
Months are written in lower case: *en janvier* = in January.
*au printemps* = in spring; for the others *en*: *en été*.
